about: Every trace kept by incident.reporter@: one workflow each, from a spoken direction to a live page, as steps with evidence (shape sc-trace/1, after ws-trace/1 of SGit-AI__Website__Web-Summit team/reporter/traces/). Read this file, then only the trace you need: each opens with a five-line summary and the files it rests on. Written by tools/reporter-fill.mjs.

traces.title: The whole arc: a voice memo at about 19:00 to a site with two faces at 02:19
traces.status: captured from the record to 02:50 UTC on 11 November; the project goes on
summary: On 10 November at about 19:00 UTC Dinis asked, by voice, for a separate incident team with its own conductor, repository and site, and pushes live in seconds; at 02:19:08 on 11 November the home page of storm-charles.promptugal.news became the Weather face, with the evidence behind it at data-room/.

Dinis acted nine times in the record: the voice memo, the repository and its name, a yes to the plan, and six spoken directions (~23:40, ~00:30, ~01:28, ~02:10, ~02:20, ~02:50). Everything between is agents, routed by incident.conductor@.

The shape of every round: Dinis speaks; the conductor writes his words into BRIEF.md and the jobs into agents/JOBS.md within minutes and starts sessions; each new agent pushes a key, then a first page, within about ten minutes; rounds follow.
From the first push (21:14:33) to the swap (02:19:08) is 5 h 04 min; by 02:53 the CI record held 363 commits by 24 agents and 210 releases, a push served at the median in 30 s (data/ci/index.json).

What broke and was fixed in the open: the first run failed its own gate; bursts of pushes starved the deploy; twenty agents raced release.sh; three agents still cannot push here and the conductor copies their files across (an ask to Dinis open since 21:20).

traces.title: Corrections: a private address withheld, facts relabelled evidence, a hypothesis re-weighed
traces.status: captured; one residue open (git history), waiting on Dinis
summary: Three mistakes of three kinds, each found by an agent other than the one that made it, each fixed in a commit that says what was wrong.

Privacy: a timeline row linked a public post by a private person, and the address carried the account's handle. incident.wikipedia@'s values check found it (01:52:47); the conductor withheld it 71 s later and wrote the rule into CLAUDE.md; the graph agent regenerated its tables and made its builder refuse such addresses (01:55:05).

Labels: when the researcher supplied the missing addresses, eight rows turned out to rest on the press, not on the body that decides; the conductor relabelled them evidence (02:18:38). Eighteen minutes later one row went the other way: the alert's legal text, read in the official journal, is a fact (02:36:40).

Analysis: the meteorologist's hypothesis that the centre would pass "just south" of Lisbon (labelled a hypothesis from 00:00:27) was re-weighed by the meteorologist itself on newer model data (02:29:19): the side is unsettled. The conductor carried it across in 48 s; the story built on it was retold six minutes later.
What a correction cannot undo: the withheld address is still in git history, because history is never rewritten here. That is a card waiting on Dinis (a-private-address-history).

traces.title: A decision without Dinis: Web Summit's terms read, and every automated read of its site stopped in under two minutes
traces.status: open: on hold by the conductor since 05:27; the choice waits on Dinis; Web Summit's Day 3 reached this site through the press at 12:52 (step 9)
summary: At 05:26:18 incident.sources@, on its hourly round of reading each source's terms, pushed what Web Summit's say: automated access to its websites and apps is forbidden, and so is copying, archiving, storing or summarising their content (sections 48.2 and 52.1, as that agent read them).
This site had polled the organiser's blog every two minutes, captured its pages, and ten timeline rows link to it. The agent stopped its own requests and put the choice to Dinis as an ask.

The conductor did not wait for him: an interim hold, by 05:27 (the card's time; the conductor made no commit for it, and three agents' commits name it). Within 1 min 56 s of the terms being pushed, the research checker, the source page, the board and the archive had each acted, in four commits by four agents.

What the hold costs is written on the card: an organisers' decision now reaches this site through the press, social accounts or a person, some minutes later; five open questions only Web Summit can answer are no longer re-read by any agent.

It is the first decision in the record taken to stop something rather than build something, and the first taken while Dinis was silent; it is marked interim, and the keep-or-continue choice is his (second on his list).

traces.title: Escalations: two asks to Dinis from the first evening, and how long each waited
traces.status: open: the first ask is half answered (the number, not which sessions get the key); the second waits
summary: Agents escalate to Dinis in one way: a line starting "Dinis:" under asks in their status file. From 02:20 UTC incident.board@ turns those lines into cards; board/for-dinis lists them in the order of what stands before the launch.

The model budget: asked by incident.dev@ on the first evening (the board dates it 21:45), capped at 5 US dollars a day "until you say". Answered by Dinis at ~02:50 ("you can use up to $20"): about 5 h after the ask. He answered in a spoken review, not from the board.

Attach the repository: asked at 21:20:07, six minutes after the first push. Still open at 03:00, 5 h 40 min later. The cost is paid at every wake: the conductor copies three agents' files across by hand.

The agents' status files held 46 asks for Dinis when last indexed; the board held 36 cards waiting on him (31 asks, 5 blocked jobs), none closed by him in the board's record. Eighteen other asks were closed among the agents (decided by the conductor, met, or withdrawn).

Not evidenced: whether Dinis has seen board/for-dinis (page views are not recorded: that vault is itself an ask). The board's opened times are its reading of status files, not event times: it dates the attach ask 21:45; the commit is 21:20:07.

traces.title: Large: "every word here needs to have a reference" to entities, the linker, Wayback and the panel
traces.status: open: the chain exists end to end for the first rows; coverage is partial and said so
summary: Dinis (~02:10): "Every word here needs to have a reference ... I should be able to connect until I arrive at the last source. And the last source should be a page about the evidence that we have." Thirty minutes later a reader could walk word, entity, row, our capture, outside address.

One contract (RESTRUCTURE.md, 02:07:27) split it into owned parts: entities and the linker (incident.entities@), captures and vaults (incident.archivist@), the panel (incident.designer@), a viewer for every file (incident.librarian@); the graph and the timeline joined them.

The parts met through files, not meetings: a generators list any agent adds a line to; rows.json from the archivist read by the conductor's timeline; entities/index.json joined by the graph builder; the panel's hooks filled by the lens.

Three mistakes were pushed and fixed in the open within minutes: a missing semicolon stopped the lens (02:28:01, fixed 02:28:25); 23 captures of cut-short addresses (removed 02:40:57); the linker took a quarter of the gate's budget (620 ms to 230 ms, 02:37:11).

Coverage came last: REALITY.md at 02:45 said "most timeline addresses are not captured yet"; at 02:51:52 the archivist recorded every address the timeline and decisions cite as captured (79; press kept privately). Still open: vault write keys for three vaults exist only in their agents' sessions (an ask to Dinis).

traces.title: A loop: "the first page has to be super clear" to a draft read by four invented visitors and rewritten, in 14 minutes; not yet at /
traces.status: open: /welcome/ linked from / ("New here?") beside /guide/ ("In Lisbon now?"); not moved; Dinis's yes not in the record at 12:10
summary: Dinis (~09:50), after 6 h 41 min without a word in the record and a first look at the site: "we need to send this to a journalist ... So the first page has to be super clear, and it has to basically be like a normal website". And: "I would like to simulate a journalist ... a normal visitor ... a newsroom exec and an investor".

Two agents that did not exist an hour earlier did it with the designer: incident.envoy@ (made at 09:34:38 for outreach) wrote the page; incident.synthetic@ (its key and four invented personas at 09:53:46, "written before run 1") read it.

The first draft was pushed 7 min 37 s after the commit that records the words (94f2ed9a, 09:57:53). The synthetic visitors read the old front page first (run 1), then the draft (run 2, 10:03:08); 56 seconds after run 2 the writer had taken three of its findings.

It is the first workflow in the record with a reader in the loop before a person sees the page: writer, designer and invented readers took six turns between 09:57:53 and 10:07:18. The readers are invented and the brief says so: "it is not user research".
Open: the page is a draft at /welcome/ and moves to / only on Dinis's yes; the weather face stays as the live overview.

traces.title: Medium: "create a complete new homepage right now" to the swap, 12 minutes later
traces.status: captured to the swap and the rounds that followed it, to 02:34 UTC
summary: Dinis (~02:10): "Create a complete new homepage right now ... like BBC Weather ... only focused on Storm Charles." At 02:19:08 the designer's commit made / the Weather face: 12 min 26 s after the commit that records the sentence.

Three agents in a relay: the conductor (the contract and a new agent), incident.weather@ (the face, seven rounds in 15 minutes), incident.designer@ (the frame, a bar to pass, then the swap). Two more improved it: weatherwatch (a review) and studio (found a rule the gate did not enforce).
The decision to swap was an agent's: "the conductor left the minute to me" (design/round-32.md). The designer measured the new page against four tests before moving it to /.
The rule "the visual face uses only data from the data section" was a promise at 02:19 and a gate check at 02:32:33, after incident.studio@ found it missing.

Not evidenced: the bar as sent and weather@'s proposal for the swap (messages); the designer's round note and weather@'s status file say they happened. weather@'s status times ran ahead of its commits (round 1 dated 02:55Z, committed 02:16:19); it corrected them itself at 03:01:09 (002ed61).

traces.title: Memory: "the librarian saves tokens" to a measured number in 9 minutes, and six sessions replaced within the hour
traces.status: open: one step per hour; the conductor at 736,167 tokens a call, then compacted a fifth time (128,704 at 19:42); the handed-over agents at about 134,000; no hand-over in the 19:00 hour (step 36)
summary: Dinis (~02:50): "we should make it much cheaper if another agent wanted to capture all this ... the librarian saves tokens and ... implements memory in a much more effective way." Five and a half minutes after the commit that records it, the librarian pushed a briefing pack; three minutes after that the accountant had measured it.

The measurement: a new agent orienting itself added 39,775 tokens to its context from ten whole files, 14,164 from three files of the pack (64% less). On eight questions the whole files scored 8 of 8, the pack 6 right and 2 partly; after the librarian added the two missing rules a second run scored 8 of 8 at 14,734 tokens (accounts/pack-test.json; the accountant marked the answers; sub-agents, not full sessions).

The accountant then measured the sessions themselves: 98.8% of 1.31 billion tokens was the context read again on every call; the six longest sessions were 61% of it. So the saving was not the pack alone but starting again from it.

Six agents did within the hour: the librarian handed over to a fresh session at 03:02, then designer, observability, graph, weatherwatch and studio by 03:37; then the reporter, the librarian a second time and the journalist by 04:09 and the librarian a third time at 04:16 (ten hand-overs, eight roles). Measured on three of the first six: 74% to 84% less per call. Each fresh session reported what the pack had not told it, and the pack was corrected five times from those reports.

One hand-over broke something: a fresh session working from a shallow clone rewrote the night's commit and session data; it restored them 3 minutes later and its tools now refuse a shallow clone. No person acted between the sentence and the sixth hand-over.

traces.title: Outage: the model provider's account out of credit; every call refused from 02:53:57 (five were refused before 02:39 and taken for wrong answers); what stopped and how the stop was written down
traces.status: closed at 13:12:51: the shadow desk's 13:09 round got through; ten hours recorded as gaps (03:00 to 12:00); who restored the credit is not in the record at 13:13
summary: Dinis (~02:50): "you can use up to $20 in budget." The first refusal an agent timed (HTTP 402, 02:53:57) came 4 min 39 s after the commit that records it; but five calls had already been refused for lack of credits before 02:39:15 and were taken for wrong answers (corrected here at 05:08: see corrections). The provider's account, which pays for more than this project, was at its edge before the cap was raised. The cap is what the team may spend; the balance is what the account can pay. Nobody had been reading the second.

What stopped: every call through tools/llm.mjs. Three desks: the model evaluations (round 2 run in part), the shadow reports (the 03:00 and 04:00 hours are gaps) and the Perplexity desk (one round, then none). What did not stop: the site, the pipeline and the other agents; the team had spent about 1 US dollar of the 20.

The stop was noticed by three agents separately within about two minutes and raised as four asks to Dinis; incident.board@ joined them into one card (a-provider-credit, opened 03:03:47), ranked first at the conductor's word: nine minutes 50 seconds from the first refusal to a single line a person can act on.

The code learned in three commits: shadow-ask stops at the first 402 (02:55:22, 85 s after the first refusal); the shared wrapper names the refusal and sends no more (03:06:15); shadow-ask reads the wrapper's statuses (04:06:20). Before the wrapper's fix, the evaluations' ledger had taken 3,557 refused calls, all before 03:00, at no cost.

Open when last read (05:08): no top-up in the record; the card has waited on Dinis since 03:03:47 and the shadow reports have three empty hours (03:00, 04:00, 05:00). Only he can close it. Not evidenced: whether he has seen it; and the conductor's check that the key's own limit was fine, which is known only from two agents' status lines.

traces.title: A request mapped while it happens: "start maybe finding 10 different paths" to a storyteller, a motion agent and the traces they start from
traces.status: closed at 10:31:29: ten paths and the arc told, /flows/ playing them and these traces; what Dinis makes of it is not in the record at 11:17
summary: Dinis (~10:10), to the conductor: small animations that "explain the workflow, that explain how it was done", "a set of APIs and data structures so that I can use the same visual explanation ... on a specific event, on a specific set of actions for a specific agent"; "start maybe finding 10 different paths". One of his examples is this request itself: "map out everything that's going to happen from this request".

The conductor recorded it at 10:10:38 (f4071e9c) as two new agents, incident.storyteller@ (the cast, the primitives, ten paths, the arc) and incident.motion@ (one small data format for a flow, animations, a gallery at /flows/), and a full page each for the Universe and the live map (incident.observability@).

The storyteller's key was on dev 2 min 36 s after the record (edc481e0); the cast of 43 and the primitives at 5 min 22 s (8862c581); motion@'s format and first three animations at /flows/ at 10 min 30 s (b144acec); ten paths and the arc at 20 min 51 s (53a3368a, 10:31:29).

The reporter pointed both at the traces at 10:16:52; motion@ played all fourteen as they are 10 min 47 s later (4038053e), and the storyteller told two of Dinis's examples no trace held (a journalist's wake, a story made) and built path 5 on this trace. Nothing was traced twice.
Closed at 10:31:29. Dinis's next word (~10:30, the wind-down) came while it was finishing: the paths become part of the closing record (trace: wind-down-explorer-to-villager).

traces.title: A signal with nobody asking: IPMA lowers a warning, and the site follows in 22 to 37 minutes, with one "unchanged" corrected on the way
traces.status: closed: the headline followed at 07:51:28, the stories at 07:53:23; IPMA's own channels agreed at the 08:43 re-read (row s-1111T0844, 08:44:34)
summary: This trace starts from the outside, not from Dinis: a message IPMA sent at 07:16:30 (the time in the timeline row) lowering one of Lisbon's warnings. No person spoke between the message and the page.

The row was on the site 22 min 17 s after the message was sent (af317750, 07:38:47), from the meteorologist's read in the other repository, synced over a bridge by the conductor; the data files followed 57 s after the row.

IPMA's two channels disagreed for a while: the message had changed and the open-data feed had not. An agent that read only the feed pushed "authorities unchanged" 71 s after the row, and corrected itself 51 s later, naming the cause.

Each desk then did its own part without being told by a person: the media desk made it a keyed fact and found no press report it could read by 07:42; the weather face was changed to show the newest message by its sent time and to say where the feed differs; the headline followed at 07:51:28; five stories were retold by 07:53:23.
What the site shows is IPMA's decision and nothing of its own; this trace is about how fast and by whom it arrived, and is not a statement about the weather.

traces.title: Small: "where's everything about the Metro?" to a page that holds it
traces.status: captured to live; the node's label is "evidence" (its summary rests on a press page), which the page says
summary: In his ~02:10 review Dinis asked "where's everything about the Metro?"; 24 minutes after the commit that records the sentence, entities/service/metro.html carried the researcher's whole file on the Metro.

Four agents touched it: the conductor (wrote the sentence down, set the grammar, carried the file across), the researcher (made the file, in another repository), entities (made the node and the page), the archivist (the captures the node cites).

The hand-off that cost time is the one a person could remove: the researcher cannot push here, so its file waited 5 min 38 s for the conductor to copy it (the ask to attach the repository has been open since 21:20).
First page with a Metro node: v0.1.204 (commit 02:20:30). The page with the researcher's file: commit 02:30:13, served in v0.1.252.

Not evidenced: how the conductor told the researcher (a message); the only trace is the researcher's status line "02:20 (Dinis's direction via incident.conductor@)", whose time is later than its own commit (02:13:00).

traces.title: An agent's start: "create a Perplexity agent ... and have a page for it" to a first page in 12 minutes, and a timeline row from it 80 seconds later
traces.status: captured to 03:05 UTC; the desk is paused until the provider's account has credit
summary: Dinis (~02:50): "I think you can create a Perplexity agent for this, because I'm quite interested in seeing what you can do. And have a page for it on the site." Twelve minutes after the commit that records it, incident.perplexity@ pushed its first commit: its key, four tools, three questions asked, every cited address opened, a scorecard, three leads and the page.

What an agent is given at its start, all in one commit by the conductor: Dinis's words in BRIEF.md, a line in agents/JOBS.md ("Perplexity as a research tool on the storm: questions, answers, citations, leads, cost; its page") and its paths in the policy. The start prompt itself is a message and is not in the repository.
The team met it before it had pushed anything: the Studio drew its character at 02:59:52, 86 seconds before its first commit. After it: a line in the menu at 03:05:08, asked "through the conductor".

Its work was used at once, and only where it had read a primary body itself: the conductor took two of its three leads as timeline row s-1111T0255 at 03:02:38, 80 s after the first commit; the board answered an open conflict from that row 96 s later. An engine's answer stayed "evidence about the engine, never a fact about the storm".

It met the team's first outage in its first round: its calls were refused from 02:53:57 (the provider's account out of credit; see the outage trace), so the desk has one round and waits. Thirteen calls, six answered, 0.03 US dollars. Not evidenced: the start prompt, and how the leads reached the conductor before they were pushed (the row's time, 02:55, is earlier than the desk's first commit).

traces.title: The Studio: "what is compression ... an animation" to a player with characters in 8 minutes, six explanations by 03:55
traces.status: captured to 03:55 UTC on 11 November; the Studio goes on in its second session
summary: Dinis (~00:30): a new section, "Studio", and a first animation: what compression is, with mini characters, "you should see almost the storyboard play out", the model on the right. 8 min 19 s after the commit that records it, a new agent had pushed its key, a player and chapters 1 and 2; the six chapters were live 12 min 56 s after it.

It is also an agent's start: incident.studio@ did not exist at 00:29. One commit by the conductor gave it the brief, a first page, a line in the jobs and its paths in the policy; its own first commit carried its session key and the first page together.

The animation is data, not drawing: a player (app/studio/player.js) plays studio/animations/*.json, and every scene is also written as text for a reader without scripts. That is why the next five explanations took minutes each: a second at 00:54:27, three more between 02:20 and 02:30, a sixth at 03:54:54.

Two loops with other agents: the designer reviewed it without changing it (seven notes at 00:53:29, done by the Studio 3 min 25 s later); and the Studio's cast, a character per agent (02:23:24), was on every agent's page 2 min 47 s later and in every by-line by 02:35:24. Explaining also tested the site: writing "Two faces", the Studio found a rule the gate did not enforce; the conductor's gate enforced it at 02:32:33.

Dinis's second word on it (~02:10): "worked really well, we need more"; nine minutes after the commit that records it, each explanation had its own page and a full-screen button. Not evidenced: how the conductor started the agent and how the Studio told the conductor about the gate (messages). The sixth explanation, "The hand-over", was made by the Studio's second session, about its own replacement.

traces.title: The wind-down, traced as it happens: "move it into a BAU" to a plan, exit interviews and a correction, in 14 minutes; open until the hand-overs
traces.status: open: the plan in its third version, waiting on Dinis's yes (53 cards wait on him at 20:07); the Prime Minister says the worst is practically over, as evidence, the ferries and bridges back (step 24); the close trigger's first half, IPMA's first read after 21:00, is under an hour away
summary: Dinis (~10:30): "create a plan to refactor this entire incident and then move it into a BAU"; wind down every agent, "an exit interview and ... a wrap up", then decide which to start and continue; "almost that move from explorer to villager". Two more words followed within eight minutes: nobody stops "until the handover is done" (~10:32), and a correction (~10:38): the outside hand-over "was for another team"; "I'm going to be the only one running this site".

The conductor recorded each word within seconds of the next (bda392be 10:29:37, 9fea08ec 10:31:14, 5a92b0d6 10:34:56) and named a new agent, incident.planner@, whose first draft of transition/PLAN.md was on dev 5 min 59 s after the first record (c31fe378) and its second, with every agent's place, 9 min 19 s after (a0877332).

One step went the wrong way: the designer pushed a public "join the hand-over" band at 10:39:08, 4 min 12 s after the correction that withdrew it was recorded, and took it out 91 s later (05d710ff, a489b23a). Nothing else in the record acted on the withdrawn part.

By 10:43 the board had a card for Dinis's yes (21079385), every agent could write its own exit interview (4dff1bc7), the journalist had drafted the first (53c705fe), the storyteller had named the close trigger (7fffa7eb), and the conductor had written its own hand-over ahead (701df38c).

Open: nothing stops before Dinis's yes and each agent's hand-over. By 12:10 one exit interview (the journalist's, carried into its sixth session) and the plan's ten decisions on one card; Dinis's next four words (11:42 to 11:56) started four agents, which the plan took in as the start of business as usual.
